name: SUMICO / Tokyo Axion Helioscope
summary: A historical Japanese solar-axion telescope extending its coherent mass reach with helium gas at different densities.
detection_principle: Solar axions convert to X-rays in a superconducting magnet; helium gas tunes the effective photon mass and PIN photodiodes measure the signal.

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 2010 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

collaboration.name: SUMICO / Tokyo Axion Helioscope Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

phases.name: Early vacuum / low-density-gas phases
phases.description: The region below approximately 0.27 eV has been explored.

phases.name: Third phase
phases.description: Mass matching with higher-density helium gas.

results.summary: No signal; 95% CL coupling upper limits of 5.6–13.4×10⁻¹⁰ GeV⁻¹ were obtained in this mass interval.

science_scope: Primarily searches for solar-produced axions or hidden photons as complementary tests of dark-matter candidates. Solar flux is distinct from cold Galactic-halo dark matter; a solar-axion discovery alone would not establish the composition of cosmic dark matter.
